findings.text: A compressed-page descriptor carries a free-object index and a size-class index; a pool holds an array of size-class descriptors each with its own lock plus deferred-free work. Dedicated helpers expose the free index and resolve the class descriptor through the pool array.
A block descriptor and a page descriptor share storage and convert by address reinterpretation qualified by constness; a frame number maps to a descriptor through the page layer.
Compressed-object handles encode a frame number, an intra-page index and a class selector using dedicated shift and mask parameters.

A handle is a memory location holding an encoded object value observed with a single volatile read; one decoding yields a descriptor plus index pair while a separate decoding yields the class selector.

Class-level mutual exclusion is acquired before relying on stable page state derived from a handle; one protocol derives the class from the encoded value and re-samples after locking, the other stabilizes page identity under a pool read lock before taking the class lock and releasing the pool lock.
Deferred freeing is requested by scheduling pool-owned work rather than freeing synchronously.

A compressed swap entry is attributed to a node derived from its own storage address and to a control group derived from its object charge when charge tracking is present, otherwise to no group; entries return to a dedicated cache and pools release through a per-CPU reference.
List LRU deletion accepts a table, an item, a node and a group, reports whether the item was linked, and leaves unlinked items untouched.

Shard locking offers plain, interrupt-disabling and flag-saving variants selected by caller-supplied mode; public lock and unlock wrappers use the plain mode while internal selection may request interrupt modes.
A list LRU comprises per-node shards, optionally extended by a group-indexed table of per-node shards; each shard carries a spin lock and an item count, with an additional node-wide atomic count.
Removal only affects linked items and maintains both shard-local and node-wide counts when removal occurs.

Fast swap allocation consults a per-CPU cached device and offset for the folio size, validates liveness and usability under the cluster lock, scans the enclosing cluster, and reports success by whether the folio became swap-cached.

Cluster usability requires a usable flag range, an allocated mapping table, and size compatibility where higher orders demand either an empty cluster or a matching exclusive order; emptiness means zero occupancy count.

A cluster moves among free, fragmented and full according to occupancy, while discard clusters stay off the normal lists; empty selects free, partial occupancy selects fragmented keyed by order, full occupancy selects full.

Cluster table presence is checked with the cluster spin lock held; cluster scanning and installation require that lock held, while device availability changes serialize under a global availability lock with the device lock additionally held for forced removal.

Reclaim temporarily releases the cluster lock while attempting folio reclaim, so on reacquisition the cluster must be rechecked for usability and the target range re-examined because concurrent allocation or freeing may have changed it.

Swap table values distinguish null, folio-backed and counted encodings; table reads use RCU with a null fallback when no table is present, count construction reserves distinct free, used and saturated representations, and frame numbers combine with flag bits and a folio marker.

Swap slots transition from empty to folio-backed at insertion with defined initial counts, and return toward empty after reclaim; cache insertion records the swap identity on the folio, raises its reference, marks swap-cache membership and updates accounting, while lookup succeeds only for folio-marked values with a live reference.

A swap-cached folio is only freed from cache when locked, still cached, not under writeback and storage is not suspended for image creation, preventing reuse of a slot already captured in a hibernation image; reclaim uses a non-blocking folio lock to avoid deadlock and revalidates identity after locking because the offset may have shifted.

Device usage accounting increments a shared in-use count and decrements a global free count; reaching capacity removes the device from the availability list once via an atomic off-list mark and schedules background reclaim, while explicit removal clears writability under both locks.
Visible helpers in this lane provide list-LRU deletion and shard lock management plus swap-cache folio lookup and insertion.

Swap management uses a fixed cluster size with aligned scanning, an invalid-entry sentinel, cluster flag and order fields, device capability and state flags, reclaim policy selectors, and an off-list usage bit with count limits.

Group-aware shard selection tolerates concurrent reparenting by retrying with the parent group when the indexed shard is absent or marked with a draining sentinel; callers may either bail out or treat missing shards as empty.
Charge-group resolution for removal and group-aware shard selection run inside RCU read sections, and swap-table reads similarly protect table dereference with RCU.
